items.short_quote: It’s important to still occasionally check your blood sugar with a fingerstick
items.comparison_quote: you'll still need to test daily with a blood sugar meter
items.issue: Same-agency educational pages differ in stated frequency. The2025 page directs readers to ask their care team how often. Date alone does not prove one page formally supersedes another. Calibration and verification remain distinct purposes.
items.suggestion: Preserve source-specific conditions and dates; device-specific instructions and professional review needed. No universal daily or never-fingerstick rule.

items.section: How to Dispose of Sharps; Importance of Safe Sharps Disposal
items.short_quote: Used sharps should be immediately placed in a sharps disposal container.
items.comparison_quote: Dispose of the lancet and strip in a trash container.
items.issue: CDC wording does not specify a sharps-safe container. FDA explicitly prohibits loose sharps in household/public trash. The CDC sentence does not explicitly instruct loose disposal, so no direct contradiction is assumed.
items.suggestion: Clarify safe container requirements, distinguish lancet from teststrip, and retain regional disposal requirements. Do not interpret trash container as permission for loose sharps. Independent professional review pending; no whole-source quarantine added.
